office_does: A State Senator writes and votes on Washington state law, the state budgets and tax policy, and confirms gubernatorial appointments, serving a four-year term.
race_blurb: Two Democratic legislators face off: Rep. Cindy Ryu, who calls incumbent Sen. Jesse Salomon too moderate, against Salomon. Both voted for the new tax on income over $1 million; they split on whether to extend it to lower incomes.

candidates.summary: State Representative since 2011 and chair of the House technology committee, challenging the incumbent senator from the left on taxes and housing.
highlights: Said in an October KUOW debate she would extend the new income tax to household incomes near $250,000, at a lower rate [S5]
Voted for ESSB 6346 (2026 income tax over $1 million) and for 2025 rent stabilization [S9][S11]
Endorsed by the 32nd District Democrats and WEA-PAC [S13][S14]

taxes.basis: Voted for the $1 million income tax and says she would extend it to households near $250,000; pamphlet asks the wealthiest to pay their share.

spending.basis: Platform centers on investing in public schools, early learning, childcare and transportation; no audit or restraint language.

housing.basis: Voted for rent stabilization and lists rent caps, homebuyer programs and social/mixed-income housing, alongside speeding construction.

climate.basis: Lists advancing renewable energy and green jobs and safeguarding the environment.

experience.basis: Sixteen years in the House, committee chair, with bills signed into law.

tech.basis: Backs AI regulation and a state privacy law, opposes data-center subsidies, and passed a 2025 law on AI-forged likenesses.

social.basis: Calls herself a proud advocate of protecting reproductive rights, decisions for patients and doctors.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, the 2025 amendments to the I-2081 parental-rights list; no campaign statement on the topic.

candidates.summary: Two-term incumbent state senator and Local Government Committee chair who supports the millionaires tax but opposes extending it, and pledges to audit spending.
highlights: Pulled SB 6346 (millionaires tax) from Senate Rules and voted for it, but calls a $250,000 threshold "incredibly out of touch" [S6][S7]
Pamphlet pledges to audit spending and expand senior property-tax relief [S1]
Endorsed by the Seattle Times (per his site), AWB and the Snohomish County Sheriff [S4][S14]

taxes.basis: Voted for and backs the $1 million income tax, but rejects extending it and says more revenue should have gone to tax relief rather than the operating budget.

spending.basis: Pamphlet says government must be more responsible with tax dollars and pledges to audit spending.

housing.basis: Wrote permitting and supply bills and also voted for rent stabilization; a genuine mix of both poles.

safety.basis: Describes a balanced enforcement-and-treatment approach, criticizing the Blake overcorrection while backing treatment, housing and officer decertification.

climate.basis: Says he sponsored the Climate Commitment Act and supported a fracking ban and clean-energy investment.

experience.basis: Incumbent senator since 2019 and committee chair with bills passed each session.

immigration.basis: Cites banning ICE face masks and co-sponsoring judicial-warrant and audit-notice protections.

healthcare.basis: Health priorities are price accountability and oversight within the existing system; no universal-coverage proposal.

social.basis: Says he is 100% pro-choice, sponsored SB 5400 shielding providers, and supports a constitutional right to reproductive care.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, the 2025 amendments to the I-2081 parental-rights list; no campaign statement on the topic.

tech.basis: Cites leading the fight to block AI-powered rent-setting schemes.
